story.title: Fire at Indonesian Confectionery Factory Leaves Three Dead and Dozens Missing
story.summary: A fire at a confectionery factory west of Jakarta, Indonesia, has resulted in at least three fatalities, with 36 individuals reported missing. The blaze, which began in a cooling unit on the third floor, has left parts of the factory severely damaged, including a collapsed roof. Firefighters continue to battle the flames more than 12 hours after the incident started, while rescue efforts are underway to locate the missing persons.

explore_lenses.label: Why is the worker count still unsettled?
explore_lenses.title: Records and contact data are being reconciled
explore_lenses.summary: The initial missing-person figure was provisional because responders were still matching company attendance information with family reports while access to parts of the plant remained restricted.

claims.text: At the morning update, Banten officials said workers' whereabouts could not yet be confirmed in part because phones had been left in lockers, limiting direct contact.
Police set up a family reporting post and said company entry-record matching was hindered because power at the site had not fully returned.

The factory's CEO said 65 workers were believed to have been in the affected area, while the company later counted 24 as home and four receiving treatment; those figures explain why the number unaccounted for could change as verification continued.

explore_lenses.label: Why is the rescue taking so long?
explore_lenses.title: Heat, fire pockets and collapsed material limit entry
explore_lenses.summary: The operation is not solely a search: crews must cool the site and assess structural safety before they can enter each section, slowing both rescue and accounting for workers.

claims.text: Banten authorities said factory raw materials could allow flames to reignite, so intensive cooling continued after the main fire was brought under control.
Officials cited partial building collapse, remaining hot areas and nighttime visibility as reasons crews could not reach all parts of the factory immediately.
Basarnas Banten said search teams were dividing the facility into sectors by safety level because debris and active fire points remained inside.

explore_lenses.label: What will establish the fire's cause?
explore_lenses.title: A forensic inquiry must wait for safe access
explore_lenses.summary: The reported origin in a third-floor cooling unit remains an account from survivors, not a confirmed official finding. Investigators first need a cooled, safe scene to examine equipment and safety systems.

claims.text: The cause was not immediately known; survivors told local media that flames began at a cooling unit on the third floor.
Banten police said they planned to bring in a forensic laboratory team on November 22, but only after the site was cool and safe for personnel.

CEO Steven Wijaya said the factory had conducted evacuation drills and had compliant, functioning routes and fire-protection systems; that is the company's account and had not been independently resolved by the announced investigation.

story_report.summary: At least three people were killed and 36 were reported missing after a fire tore through a confectionery factory west of Jakarta, Indonesia. The blaze was reported to have begun in a cooling unit on the third floor, though authorities had not established an official cause. More than 12 hours after the fire began, firefighters were still working at the site, where parts of the factory were severely damaged. Rescue teams continued efforts to locate those unaccounted for as access to the structure remained limited.

sections.heading: Worker accounting remains incomplete
sections.body: Officials said workers’ whereabouts could not yet be confirmed partly because some had left their phones in lockers, limiting direct contact. Police opened a reporting post for families, while matching workers to company entry records was hampered by incomplete restoration of power at the site. The company said 65 workers were believed to have been in the affected area; it later counted 24 at home and four receiving treatment, meaning the number unaccounted for could change as checks continue.

sections.heading: Damage complicates rescue operations
sections.body: Authorities said combustible factory raw materials could allow the fire to reignite, requiring intensive cooling even after the main blaze was brought under control. Partial building collapse, hot areas and poor nighttime visibility prevented crews from immediately reaching all parts of the factory. Basarnas Banten said search teams were dividing the building into sectors according to safety conditions because debris and active fire points remained inside.

sections.heading: Investigation awaits safer conditions
sections.body: Banten police said a forensic laboratory team was expected to examine the site only after it had cooled and was safe for personnel. The factory’s CEO, Steven Wijaya, said evacuation drills had been held and that escape routes and fire-protection systems were compliant and functioning. That account has not been independently resolved by the investigation.

unresolved.text: Authorities had not issued a final reconciled list of people in the affected area or a final casualty count.
It remained unclear when every part of the damaged factory would be safe for search teams to enter.
No official cause, determination of fire-safety-system performance, or finding of responsibility had been released.

related_stories.summary: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has condemned a series of arson attacks on Palestinian villages in the occupied West Bank, labeling them as 'Jewish terrorism.' The attacks involved Israeli settlers setting fire to vehicles and properties in multiple locations. In response, Israeli authorities have initiated an investigation into the incidents.

related_stories.title: Capture of Cartel Leader 'El Chapo Isidro' Sparks Violence in Sinaloa
related_stories.summary: Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as 'El Chapo Isidro' and one of the FBI's most wanted fugitives, was captured by Mexican special forces in Sinaloa during a military operation. Following his arrest, violence erupted in the region, resulting in at least 11 deaths, with reports of gunfire and chaos among civilians. The operation involved cooperation with US intelligence and included a shootout between security forces and armed members of his cartel.

related_stories.title: FBI Investigates Possible Hack of National Crime Information Center Database
related_stories.summary: The FBI is reportedly investigating a potential hack of the National Crime Information Center (NCIC) database, which is utilized by various law enforcement agencies to share critical criminal justice information. The NCIC contains records on fugitives, missing persons, and stolen property, among other data.
